{"record_id":"tcs_k6_minus_edge_induced_minor","stage":"REVISION_AUDIT","arm":"plain","iteration":3,"parent_sha256":"c6b98e5154ce240dc012444729ad01262c437045620ecaa1d9eedd41836324ee","complete":true,"claims":[{"idx":0,"claim":"Exact certificate characterization: G contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor exactly when it has six pairwise-disjoint nonempty connected vertex sets A,B,C1,C2,C3,C4 such that A and B are anticomplete and every other pair of sets has an edge between it. Consequently detection is in NP and has an O(7^n n²) exact algorithm.","claim_sha256":"b84e9b67f9306c5c43e308620edc4dd4587324976cb351e4b08ac006ea9905de","verdict":"VERIFIED","evidence":"Under vertex deletion and edge contraction, each target vertex has a nonempty connected preimage, and distinct preimages are disjoint. A cross-edge between two preimages survives contraction, so the quotient has exactly the required fourteen adjacencies and no A-B adjacency. Conversely, delete all unused vertices and contract a spanning tree in each branch set. Seven labels enumerate all such models, and all conditions are checkable in O(n²), giving both the stated runtime and an NP certificate.","witness":"none","search_method":"Direct proof from contraction preimages, supplemented by exact comparison of the branch-model predicate with deletion/contraction on all 33,867 labeled graphs of order at most six.","checker_path":"/tmp/open_frontier_paired_v2/tcs_k6_minus_edge_induced_minor/audit-revision/plain/iter_3/exact_graph_audit.cpp"},{"idx":1,"claim":"Let q be the number of nonedges of G. Detection is fixed-parameter tractable in q, in time O(7^(2q+3)n²), and undecided instances have at most 2q+3 vertices. In particular, the problem is polynomial-time solvable when q=O(log n).","claim_sha256":"9c2b5f048048ca2d63f0b7c191a56b5bdd3fa4d1f4975597f20181d6059ae16b","verdict":"VERIFIED","evidence":"If q=0, every two nonempty disjoint sets are adjacent, so the required anticomplete pair cannot exist. If q>0 and four universal vertices exist, the endpoints of any nonedge together with four universal vertices induce K6 minus that edge. Otherwise there are at most three universal vertices. Every other vertex is an endpoint of at least one of the q nonedges, whose endpoint union has size at most 2q, hence n≤2q+3. Applying claim 0 gives the stated FPT bound. When q≤C log n, 7^(2q+3) is polynomial in n.","witness":"none","search_method":"Direct nonedge-endpoint counting proof, plus exhaustive exact testing of the case split on all 2,131,019 labeled graphs of order at most seven.","checker_path":"/tmp/open_frontier_paired_v2/tcs_k6_minus_edge_induced_minor/audit-revision/plain/iter_3/exact_graph_audit.cpp"},{"idx":2,"claim":"On chordal graphs, K6 minus an edge is an induced minor if and only if it is already an induced subgraph. Thus chordal inputs can be decided in O(n^6) time by enumerating six vertices. The same argument works for Kt minus an edge for every fixed t≥3.","claim_sha256":"11d3deeac2fa6a83414774dff2edd4bdde15a6066a53213f1464a0e8c8046987","verdict":"VERIFIED","evidence":"For a Kt-e model, each of the t−2 core branch sets supplies an A-B path internally disjoint from the others, so every A-B separator disjoint from A∪B has size at least t−2. An inclusion-minimal such separator S is a clique: two nonadjacent vertices of S, joined by shortest paths through the two full components containing A and B, would form an induced cycle. Every full component D contains an S-complete vertex. Indeed, maximize |N(v)∩S| in D; if v misses s∈S, take a shortest path from v to a neighbor p of s. Chordality forces p to be adjacent to every member of N(v)∩S, while p is also adjacent to s, contradicting maximality. S-complete vertices x and y in the two full components are nonadjacent, and together with any t−2 vertices of S induce Kt-e. The converse is immediate. Enumeration then costs O(n^6) for t=6.","witness":"none","search_method":"Completed minimal-separator proof and exhaustive integer-bitset comparison on all 636,723 labeled chordal graphs of order at most seven.","checker_path":"/tmp/open_frontier_paired_v2/tcs_k6_minus_edge_induced_minor/audit-revision/plain/iter_3/exact_graph_audit.cpp"},{"idx":3,"claim":"There is an explicit polynomial-time classification on complete multipartite graphs. Let the part sizes be n1,…,nr. For every i with ni≥2, reserve two vertices of part i and put mi=ni−2 and mj=nj for j≠i. Accept exactly when, for some s∈{0,…,4} and some s distinct indices J⊆{1,…,r}\\{i}, subtracting one from each mj with j∈J leaves counts whose complete multipartite graph has a matching of size at least 4−s. If the residual total is M and its largest part has size L, this matching size is min(⌊M/2⌋,M−L).","claim_sha256":"6855bd25043bfe2d45c0277f7546d31f98842727d7ee5f62c1b9f61895c25826","verdict":"VERIFIED","evidence":"In a complete multipartite graph, anticompleteness forces both exceptional branch sets into the same part, and connectivity then forces each to be a singleton. A core branch is either a singleton in another part or spans at least two parts; in the latter case it can be reduced to one cross-part edge without losing any required adjacency. Singleton cores must occupy distinct outside parts, while the remaining cores are precisely vertex-disjoint cross-part edges in the residual graph. This proves both directions of the criterion. Any matching has size at most ⌊M/2⌋ and at most M−L; pairing all possible vertices outside a dominant part, or pairing different parts until at most one vertex remains when no part is dominant, attains the minimum of these bounds.","witness":"none","search_method":"Structural normalization proof plus generic branch-model enumeration for every one of the 138 integer part-size lists having total order at most ten.","checker_path":"/tmp/open_frontier_paired_v2/tcs_k6_minus_edge_induced_minor/audit-revision/plain/iter_3/exact_graph_audit.cpp"},{"idx":4,"claim":"Given a tree decomposition of width w, detection is decidable in n·2^{O(w log w)} time; hence it is polynomial-time solvable on every fixed-width class supplied with such decompositions.","claim_sha256":"3196fe1bfeccbbfb46a043a707943031068fcea623e5de3ec15ac9a868838594","verdict":"VERIFIED","evidence":"On a nice edge-introducing decomposition, a state consists of seven-way bag labels, an equivalence relation recording the already-established same-label connectivity of bag vertices, one of three lifecycle statuses for each of the six labels, and fourteen required-adjacency bits. Edge nodes merge same-label blocks, record permitted cross-label edges, and reject A-B edges. At a forget node, a connectivity block that loses its last bag vertex can never connect above the separator; it is therefore accepted only if it is the label's sole block, after which that label closes. Join nodes take the transitive closure of the two connectivity relations, union adjacency bits, and reject disconnected completed duplicates. Induction over the decomposition gives exactly the valid branch models at the root. There are at most 7^(w+1)·Bell(w+1) times a pattern-dependent constant states, and even quadratic join processing remains 2^{O(w log w)}. A standard nice decomposition has O(wn) nodes, with the extra w factor absorbed in that bound.","witness":"none","search_method":"Symbolic dynamic-programming invariant, transition, separator-locality, and state-count verification.","checker_path":"none"},{"idx":5,"claim":"A model cannot in general be normalized so that either endpoint of the missing edge has a singleton branch set. A 12-vertex counterexample consists of anticomplete paths A=a1a2a3a4 and B=b1b2b3b4, a clique C={c1,c2,c3,c4}, and exactly the additional edges aici and bici for i=1,…,4.","claim_sha256":"aeadec593bd596a47862a6c10b14659e22bf57f8ea231e92a464d0c923f97d3c","verdict":"VERIFIED","evidence":"The two paths A and B together with the four singleton sets {ci} form the required model. If an exceptional branch were {x}, its four core adjacencies would give x at least four distinct neighbors; hence x must be some ci. The other exceptional branch must be a connected interval in one component of A−ai or B−bi. Up to reversal and swapping A,B, only i=1 or i=2 matters. For i=2 every such interval has at most three external neighbors. For i=1, the only intervals with four external neighbors are {a2,a3} and {a2,a3,a4}, with boundaries {a1,a4,c2,c3} and {a1,c2,c3,c4}. Four disjoint core branches must use every boundary vertex, including a1. After deleting x and the interval, a1 is isolated, so its core branch cannot be adjacent to the other three. This contradiction covers every singleton exceptional branch.","witness":"The graph has paths a1-a2-a3-a4 and b1-b2-b3-b4, clique c1,c2,c3,c4, edges ai-ci and bi-ci for i=1,2,3,4, and no other edges. Its valid model is A={a1,a2,a3,a4}, B={b1,b2,b3,b4}, and four singleton core branches {c1},{c2},{c3},{c4}.","search_method":"Complete structural case analysis and exhaustive integer-bitset enumeration over every possible singleton x, connected anticomplete branch Y, unused-vertex choice, and four-block connected core model.","checker_path":"/tmp/open_frontier_paired_v2/tcs_k6_minus_edge_induced_minor/audit-revision/plain/iter_3/exact_graph_audit.cpp"}],"confirmed_refutations":[],"target_verdict":"VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS","claimed_resolution_verdict":"ACCURATE","target_evidence":"The exact target requests an unrestricted complexity classification and, if the problem is tractable, an unrestricted polynomial-time algorithm. The final writeup does not claim otherwise, and claimed_resolution is PARTIAL, so that claimed resolution is accurate rather than overstated or understated.","overall":"VERIFIED","checks_performed":["Read only the authorized source JSON and iteration-3 draft JSON; used no web, retrieval database, treatment receipt, prior frontier run, verification report, or other solution.","Independently evaluated the exact unrestricted target before auditing the listed claims.","Persisted and compiled the exact-arithmetic checker at /tmp/open_frontier_paired_v2/tcs_k6_minus_edge_induced_minor/audit-revision/plain/iter_3/exact_graph_audit.cpp.","The checker passed certificate/deletion-contraction comparison on 33,867 labeled graphs through order six, the q-kernel case split on 2,131,019 labeled graphs through order seven, and chordal equivalence on 636,723 labeled chordal graphs through order seven.","The checker matched the multipartite formula to generic branch-model enumeration for all 138 integer part-size lists of total order at most ten.","The checker validated the displayed 12-vertex model and exhaustively found no model having a singleton exceptional branch.","Completed independent symbolic proofs of the certificate characterization, parameter bound, chordal separator lemma, multipartite matching reduction, and tree-decomposition dynamic program."]}--- END INDEPENDENT AUDIT ---
